_note: The second heart events (data/events/heart_<villager>_5.json): one scene per villager when their heart band first reaches 5 and the farmer talks to them, after the band 3 one. One part per villager, started at its id. Our own scenes.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: There you are. I was just writing to my son in the city. He writes back twice a year, if the rice is good.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: I told him the old farm has someone in it again. That the lamp is lit in the evenings and the field is turned.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: I hope you don't mind. An old woman likes to have news to send.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: ...The children here call me Grandma. You could too, if it wouldn't feel strange.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Well. Then I'll put that in the letter too. Mind you eat properly, grandchild.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Ha! Straight as a bamboo pole. I like that better, truth be told.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: I saw it! The black carp, this morning, right under the willow. It looked at me!

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: I had my net and everything. And then I just... didn't. It looked too old to bother.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: Don't tell anyone I went soft. I'll catch something worse to make up for it.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: I had my net and I didn't use it. You promised, so I thought I should keep it too. Partners, right?

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: Hey... when I'm big, could I farm too? Mum says the field is hard work. Is it?

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: Hard, and worth it. Come help at harvest and see.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: Really? I'm bringing my own basket. A big one!

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Look what came in the post. Paint! Real lacquer red, for the sign over the door.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Father's lettering has nearly worn away. I used to think repainting it would be like rubbing him out.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: But a store that looks tired makes people walk past. And I'm not minding it anymore. It's mine now.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Which should go on the new sign, do you think?

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: The old name. Yes. He'd grumble about my brushwork either way.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Mine? ...I was hoping somebody would say that, so I didn't have to.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Thank you. You're the first person I asked. Somehow it had to be you.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: Hold out your hand. No, the other one.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: A door bell. Iron, folded nine times, cooled in snow water. It rings a little lower than you'd think.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: My teacher hung one on this smithy the day I opened it. Said a house with a bell is a house people come back to.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: I've only made three. One for my teacher's grave, one for this door. And now that one.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: I'll hang it where I hear it every morning.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: Good. ...Don't make a fuss. Go on, the field won't hoe itself.
